A minimum of 1 year of relevant expericence, preferably in an academic or scientific environment.

The Facilities Coordinator role is responsible for supporting the day-to-day facilities operations across multiple Health Sciences spaces and buildings. The ideal candidate possesses strong organizational and communication skills, along with a working understanding of facilities and safety compliance. The incumbent participates in project planning, triages general maintenance and specialized facility systems issues, and manages incoming requests via email, phone, and ticketing systems, resolving or escalating issues as needed. The incumbent coordinates facilities projects from start to finish, maintains supply inventories, and works with onsite contractors, vendors, and campus stakeholders to coordinate schedules, facilitate emergency access, and track work progress. In addition, the incumbent will conduct regular rounds to inspect for safety and security hazards, support safety compliance and emergency preparedness efforts, and maintain building access control systems and records. They will also serve as a responsive point of contact for faculty, staff, and management, communicating updates, documenting recurring issues and resolutions, drafting emails, memos, and notices, and providing onsite support for meetings and events, some occurring after hours or on weekends. The incumbent also provides backup coverage and performs other duties as assigned. This position reports fully onsite Monday through Friday.
Demonstrated attention to detail and accuracy in daily work
Working knowledge of practices and procedures relating to facility maintenance.
Working knowledge of practices and procedures of safety and emergency preparedness.
Written communication skills to prepare a variety of correspondence, reports, policies and procedures, and training documents.
Excellent organizational and time-management skills, including the ability to manage multiple concurrent requests, competing priorities, and recurring tasks.
Active listening, interpersonal communication and problem-solving skills to effectively resolve questions, concerns, issues or problems and ensure cooperative and productive working relationships.
Skills to work independently and as part of a team.
Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality.
Working organizational skills to work on multiple projects with competing deadlines, to establish goals and workload priorities, and to meet project deadlines within budget and time constraints.
Ability to troubleshoot routine operational issues and coordinate effectively with vendors and service providers.
